description: Reusable .NET 10 package that wraps ASP.NET Core Identity with cookie and JWT auth, Google OAuth, a pluggable e-mail provider, a multi-tenant model with dynamic RBAC (roles + module permissions), and secure defaults — wired up with a single AddMyIdentity call. JWT and Google OAuth secrets are supplied by the consumer (never shipped in the package).
releaseNotes: v5.1.0: an optional sign-in audit log, and two security fixes that apply with the audit on or off. Not auditing needs no migration: ApplyMyIdentityAuditModel() is called by none of the library's own model methods. To audit, call it in OnModelCreating, add one migration and set MyIdentity:Audit:Enabled; RetentionDays (1 to 36500) purges rows once a day. Adds MyIdentitySecurityEvent, MyIdentityAuditOptions (MyIdentityOptions.Audit), IMyIdentitySecurityEventSink (a sink of your own wins; then retention is yours), IMyIdentitySecurityEventService with MyIdentitySecurityEventQuery and MyIdentitySecurityEventPage (a SystemAdmin reads all rows, a TenantAdmin only their tenant's), and the constants MyIdentitySecurityEventTypes, MyIdentitySignInMethods and MyIdentitySecurityEventReasons. The audit fails open (a failed write is logged and never changes a sign-in), the secret an entry verifies is never stored, and the second step of Identity's two-factor sign-in is recorded through the SignInManager the library registers. The audit changes no public response of the library's own entries, except that with the audit on a cancelled token can surface as OperationCanceledException from the recording, after the operation's effect, and that with the audit on LogoutAsync authenticates the cookie before signing out, so a cookie whose security stamp no longer validates can also have Identity clear the two-factor remember-me cookie when the request had not authenticated the cookie already. The security fixes: through that SignInManager, a recovery code now fails closed for a locked-out or refused account (NotAllowed or LockedOut instead of Success, the code not spent); and the base of an e-mail confirmation link (RegisterAsync, SendEmailConfirmationAsync, ResendEmailConfirmationAsync) is judged by the password-reset callback's rule, before any token and before RegisterAsync writes the account, so without MyIdentity:General:PublicBaseUrl it must use https and the request's host, and is refused where there is no request (CallbackUrlHostUnverifiable). Set the option and pass IMyIdentityConfigurationService.PublicBaseUrl() or a blank base (which now takes the option), never NavigationManager.BaseUri; a startup warning names the option when it is missing outside Development. Also (MI-23): the verifySucceeded of a nested IMyIdentityUnitOfWork.ExecuteAsync that joins a unit now counts in that unit's verification, after the marks and before the work runs again, and the unit's verifications must agree, or the call that opened the unit throws InvalidOperationException (RetryLimitExceededException around it, under a strategy whose ShouldRetryOn takes it). Upgrading from 5.0.1: MyIdentity/UPGRADE.md §44; from 4.6.0: §42 and §43 first, then §44.
title: Kerberos.MyIdentity
